text:
sam: Planning to enable a bucket policy that denies any PutObject to backup buckets unless SSE=aws:kms and the request includes `x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id`. Rolling this Friday 01:30 UTC. Need quick callouts on RBAC and audit coverage.
mira: Important: Are we also restricting who can call kms:CreateGrant on the backup CMK? If not, an attacker could still create a grant and decrypt.
jack (jax): small nit: our DB snapshotter does multipart uploads and the agent historically forgot to set SSE header on the final CompleteMultipartUpload for >5GB files. Need to validate the multipart client flow.
sec-lead: Two areas: (A) prevent unencrypted PUTs (bucket policy), (B) harden KMS key policy + IAM so CreateGrant/RetireGrant only allowed by a small admin role, and require `aws:RequestTag/ticket` for auditing.
forensics-bot: Checklist for rollout: 1) run detection query for PutObject without SSE in last 30d, 2) simulate assume-role flows for cross-account restore principals, 3) pre-seed grants only for allowlisted tenants during canary, 4) alert on any Decrypt AccessDenied after change.
sam: Good. Mira can you paste the bucket policy snippet you propose? I'll attach to the CHG.
mira: snippet (will attach as policy):
```json
{
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Principal": "*",
  "Action": "s3:PutObject",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::rd-backups-*/*",
  "Condition": {
    "StringNotEquals": {
      "s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms",
      "s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/rd-backups-key"
    }
  }
}
```
jax: For multipart, test script: create a 6GB file and run our snapshot upload to staging. Verify head-object shows `ServerSideEncryption: aws:kms`. If not, agent needs patch.
sec-lead: KMS policy suggestion (human-readable): allow kms:CreateGrant only for `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-grant-admin` and require `aws:RequestTag.chg_id` present. Deny CreateGrant from other principals. Also emit CloudWatch metric when CreateGrant occurs.
infra-bot: Example CLI to list grants for the CMK: `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/rd-backups`
forensics-bot: Detection queries I recommend: CloudTrail pseudo-query to find PUTs without SSE: 
```
SELECT eventTime, userIdentity.arn, requestParameters.bucketName, requestParameters.key
FROM cloudtrail_events
WHERE eventName = 'PutObject' AND NOT requestParameters.headers LIKE '%x-amz-server-side-encryption%'
  AND requestParameters.bucketName LIKE 'rd-backups-%'
ORDER BY eventTime DESC
LIMIT 200
```
sam: Canary plan: 30m window in staging, run 3 restores (same-account, cross-account, cross-region) and 3 snapshot uploads, pre-seed grants for the cross-account restore roles, monitor Decrypt AccessDenied and AssumeRoleDenied. Abort if any restore attempts fail.
mira: How do we pre-seed a grant for the canary? Example: `aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/rd-backups --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::210987654321:role/tenant-restore --operations Decrypt --name canary-tenant-restore`
jax: Also add an integrity check post-restore (checksum) not just success code. We've had silent corruption before.
sec-lead: Alert rules: (1) CloudWatch metric filter for `Decrypt AccessDenied` on rd-backups key; page sec-oncall if >0 in 10m during canary. (2) Metric for `PutObject` without SSE in backup buckets; page infra if >0 in 5m.
forensics-bot: Also ensure CloudTrail is logging `requestParameters.headers` for PutObject events; some log sinks truncate headers and you lose SSE header visibility.
infra-bot: We should run `aws s3api head-object` after test uploads to assert `ServerSideEncryption` and `SSEKMSKeyId`. Scriptable assert below:
```bash
H=$(aws s3api head-object --bucket rd-backups-staging --key test-snap)
if echo "$H" | grep -q 'ServerSideEncryption'; then echo ok; else echo MISSING_SSE; fi
```
sam: Rollback plan: 1) revert bucket policy, 2) revoke pre-seeded grants, 3) remove any partial updates to key policies if applied (we will stage key policy changes separately), 4) open an incident if any customer data was exposed. Document steps in CHG.
mira: One more caveat: if we deny PutObject without SSE, signed URLs from legacy clients may fail. We should scan for pre-signed URL usage patterns and talk to teams owning them.
jax: I can run a scan for recent `GetObject` events where userAgent contains `aws-sdk` and source IPs external to our datacenter; might indicate presigned URLs in the wild.
sec-lead: Post-change hardening: require `kms:ViaService` condition when CreateGrant is called from EC2? Not always possible. Better to require `aws:RequestTag/chg_id` and only allow CreateGrant from the admin role. Also add an org-wide detector for any CreateGrant on backup CMKs.
forensics-bot: I'll run a historical scan and produce a CSV of any non-SSE PutObject events in the last 90 days and flag top uploader principals. Attaching to I-3812346789.
infra-bot: I'll add canary dashboard tiles: PutObject-no-sse count, Decrypt-AccessDenied count, AssumeRoleDenied count for backup roles.
sam: Owners: jax -> multipart upload test + checksum script; mira -> bucket policy + key policy draft; infra-bot -> dashboards and pre-seed script; forensics-bot -> historical scan; sec-lead -> alerting and gating. Planning staging canary Thu 02:00 UTC. Will attach CHG.
sec-lead: One final ask: tag any pre-seeded grants with `temporary=true` and `chg_id=CHG-3812346789` and auto-expire them after 1h. We must not leave grants dangling.
forensics-bot: Noted. I'll include grant TTL verification in the canary checklist.
sam: Thanks team. Post canary results here. "
